questions.question: Autoimmune encephalitis is primarily characterized as an inflammatory disorder mediated by:
questions.detail: Autoimmune encephalitis is an antibody-mediated inflammatory disorder that typically affects the limbic system.

questions.question: In the classification of autoimmune encephalitis, Group I antibodies are distinguished from Group II antibodies because they target:
questions.detail: The primary distinction is their target: Group I antibodies target intracellular antigens, while Group II target cell surface antigens.

questions.question: Which clinical feature is most characteristic of Group I antibody-mediated autoimmune encephalitis?
choices: Close association with paraneoplastic syndromes and worse clinical outcomes
Predominant occurrence in children following vaccination
Lack of any imaging abnormalities in most cases
questions.detail: Group I antibodies are strongly linked to underlying malignancies (paraneoplastic) and typically have worse outcomes due to irreversible neuronal damage and poor response to therapy.

questions.question: What is the most common paraneoplastic form of autoimmune encephalitis?
questions.detail: Anti-Hu is the most frequent paraneoplastic form and is most commonly associated with small-cell lung cancer.

questions.question: Typical MRI findings for Anti-Hu encephalitis include hyperintense lesions on FLAIR sequences located in the:
questions.detail: Imaging for Anti-Hu characteristically shows hyperintense FLAIR signal in the medial temporal lobes, sometimes involving the cerebellum and brainstem.

questions.question: Which Group I antibody is characteristically associated with testicular germ cell tumors?
questions.detail: Anti-Ma/Ta has a strong association with testicular cancer, whereas Anti-CV2 is often associated with malignant thymoma.

questions.question: Although classified as a Group I antibody, which of the following is NOT typically associated with an underlying malignancy?
choices: All Group I antibodies are paraneoplastic
questions.detail: Anti-GAD (glutamic acid decarboxylase) is an exception among Group I antibodies as it is not typically associated with malignancy.

questions.question: Non-paraneoplastic encephalitis associated with Group II antibodies is most commonly associated with:
questions.detail: Patients with Group II non-paraneoplastic encephalitis often develop symptoms following vaccination, a viral infection, or in the context of another autoimmune disorder.

questions.question: What is the most common form of Group II (non-paraneoplastic) encephalitis, classically seen in young women and children?
questions.detail: NMDAr encephalitis is the most common non-paraneoplastic form and frequently affects young women and pediatric populations.

questions.question: Which imaging characteristic is 'unique' to the initial clinical presentation of NMDAr encephalitis?
choices: Immediate thick ring enhancement in the temporal lobes
The majority of patients have no imaging abnormalities initially
Dense calcification of the basal ganglia
Symmetric restricted diffusion in the thalami
questions.detail: NMDAr encephalitis is unique because initial imaging is often normal. Later, FLAIR hyperintensities may appear in the insular cortex, cingulate gyrus, and temporal lobes.
